fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles so responding units can reach both the main residence and the detached structure without obstruction.
• Mark or post the address on the detached structure so responders can identify it as a separate building on arrival.
• Trim any vegetation along the side of the property that limits movement between the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep a pedestrian path between the two structures clear and unobstructed for responder foot access.
• Identify and communicate the single access point to local fire and EMS so they can pre-plan approach and staging before an emergency occurs.
• Designate a clear staging area within the open green space for responding units, and keep that area free of stored equipment or debris.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Clear brush and shrubs along the rear of the property to allow firefighter movement and access behind the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to reduce the chance of fire moving from tree to tree toward the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly adjacent to the structure on all visible sides.
• Cut ground vegetation back from the base of the structure to create bare or short-mowed separation.
• Trim overhanging tree branches that extend over or close to the roofline.
• Keep the single driveway access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs along its full length.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear travel path for vehicles.
• Thin brush concentrations visible near any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Separate scattered shrubs from each other and from trees to reduce continuous pathways for fire moving across the ground toward the structure.
